contentHtml:
KENYA— AGC Tenwek Hospital has successfully performed what it says is Kenya’s first keyhole surgery on a newborn, marking a significant milestone in the country’s pediatric surgical care.

The procedure was led by Dr. Daniel Tamirat Cherkos, a consultant pediatric surgeon at the hospital, who worked with a multidisciplinary surgical team to perform the minimally invasive operation on the newborn.

Milestone in pediatric surgery

Keyhole surgery, also known as minimally invasive surgery, involves making small incisions through which surgeons insert specialized instruments and a camera to perform an operation.

Compared with conventional open surgery, the technique can reduce surgical trauma and may support faster recovery.

Performing such a procedure on a newborn requires highly specialized surgical expertise because of the patient’s small size and the technical challenges associated with operating on delicate tissues and organs.

Tenwek Hospital congratulated Dr. Cherkos and the surgical team for successfully completing the procedure and described the achievement as an important advancement in pediatric surgical care in Kenya.

The hospital said the milestone reflects the team’s dedication to improving treatment options for some of the country’s youngest and most vulnerable patients.

Advancing specialized care

According to the hospital, the achievement resulted from extensive preparation, technical expertise and a commitment to introducing innovative approaches to surgical care.

Dr. Cherkos and his colleagues have worked to expand access to specialized pediatric surgical services, with the latest procedure demonstrating the potential for advanced minimally invasive techniques to be used in newborn care.

The hospital praised the team for combining surgical skill with careful planning and a commitment to patient safety.

“Behind this milestone is not just surgical skill, but countless hours of dedication, courage, innovation and an unwavering commitment to the smallest and most vulnerable patients entrusted to your care,” the hospital said.

The successful operation also highlights the growing capacity of Kenyan healthcare institutions to undertake complex procedures that require highly specialized expertise and advanced surgical techniques.

Recognition for the surgical team

Tenwek Hospital said Dr. Cherkos’ leadership played a central role in achieving the milestone, while also recognizing the contribution of the wider surgical team involved in the procedure.

The hospital described the achievement as the result of teamwork, professional dedication, and a willingness to push the boundaries of what is possible in pediatric medicine.

It also commended the team for providing care to a newborn who required specialized surgical intervention, emphasizing the importance of innovation in improving outcomes for children and their families.

“On behalf of the entire Tenwek Hospital family, we celebrate you, the incredible surgical team, and this historic achievement,” the hospital said.

The hospital further expressed its appreciation to Dr. Cherkos and the entire team for their contribution to advancing pediatric surgical care in Kenya.

The procedure adds to the range of specialized services available at AGC Tenwek Hospital and underscores the institution’s focus on developing advanced surgical capabilities for patients requiring complex care.
